question: Who among the following was the successor of Mughal emperor Shahjahan to the throne?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Aurangzeb**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aurangzeb, **the** successor of Mughal emperor Shah Jahan**, ascended to the throne after a succession struggle among his four sons in 1657.
 
• He declared himself emperor in 1658, succeeding Shah Jahan, who had fallen ill.
 
• Despite Shah Jahan's recovery from illness, Aurangzeb emerged victorious and imprisoned him in the Agra Fort until his death in 1666.
 
• Aurangzeb ruled the Mughal Empire from **1658 to 1707, **marking a significant period in Indian history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mirza Shahab-ud-Din Muhammad Khurram, **also known as** Shah Jahan I, **was the **fifth Mughal Emperor,** reigning from 1628 until 1658.
 
• His rule marked the pinnacle of the Mughal Empire's architectural and cultural achievements.
 
• As the third son of Jahangir, Shah Jahan actively participated in military campaigns against the Sisodia Rajputs of Mewar and the rebellious Lodi nobles of the Deccan.
 
• Upon Jahangir's death in October 1627, Shah Jahan emerged victorious in a power struggle against his youngest brother, Shahryar Mirza, and ascended to the throne, crowning himself emperor in the Agra Fort.
